findings: Arjovsky et al. define W1 on compact metric X and invoke, but do not prove, compact Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality; Cat4 now reuses P-KR-01/02 rather than proposing duplicate W1/KR items.

Theorem 1 gives continuity for continuous generator maps and local Lipschitz continuity/a.e. differentiability when g is locally Lipschitz with E[L(theta,Z)] finite. Theorem 3’s ideal-critic gradient additionally requires an attaining 1-Lipschitz critic and well-defined derivative/exchange conditions.

The neural WGAN algorithm is an approximation: weight clipping is explicitly called a poor Lipschitz enforcement method, and neither approximate critics nor saddle-point convergence/mode collapse are theorem consequences.

findings: Papamakarios et al. use an equal-dimensional global diffeomorphism T:R^D→R^D with both T and T^{-1} differentiable; the density formula is exactly the C1 change-of-variables theorem with |det DT^{-1}|, and compositions multiply Jacobian determinants/add log determinants.

The triangular conditional-CDF construction requires a target density positive everywhere and differentiable conditional CDFs in current and preceding coordinates; positive conditional density makes each scalar CDF strictly increasing, and the base must satisfy the analogous regularity to map through the uniform cube.
The source states representational existence only; it does not establish finite neural approximation, optimization, or direct representation of discrete/singular-manifold laws.

source_evidence.source_claims: Equal-dimensional global differentiable bijection with differentiable inverse gives transformed density using the absolute Jacobian determinant; composition adds log-Jacobian terms. A triangular conditional-CDF construction represents positive sufficiently smooth densities under its assumptions. For continuous flows, state-Lipschitz continuous-time vector fields yield unique trajectories and log-density evolves as minus the divergence integral.
source_evidence.hypotheses_and_proof_scope: Density change is the ordinary Euclidean change-of-variables theorem for a global C1 diffeomorphism. source_evidence.source_limits: Representational existence is not finite-network approximation or trainability. Full-dimensional smooth density models do not directly represent discrete or singular-manifold laws; continuous-flow numerical integration and adjoint gradients are approximations.

library_supplier_contracts.contract: For open U,V⊂R^n and a C1 diffeomorphism T:U→V, the nonnegative Lebesgue-measurable change-of-variables identity holds; explicitly assumes Countable Choice.
For a square-dimensional C1 map, Jacobian determinant is det(DT); the change-of-variables volume factor is its absolute value.
D det(A)[H]=tr(adj(A)H) for every square matrix; on invertible A, Jacobi’s formula is det(A)tr(A^{-1}H).

findings: Chen et al. define the adjoint and instantaneous-change equations, but the Appendix A proof uses Taylor/Jacobian derivative exchanges from Lipschitz assumptions without a sufficient differentiability argument. The scaffold now replaces that step with a local C-infinity flow proof.

The local theorem assumes joint C-infinity dependence, uniform global state-Lipschitz and compact-parameter origin bounds on a finite interval; published global ODE and smooth-parameter-dependence results give a global diffeomorphic flow and C1 Jacobian.

The determinant ODE and density formula follow from the variational equation, Jacobi’s formula on invertible J, and the published nonnegative change-of-variables theorem. No consulted source supplies general numerical solver convergence or equality of continuous adjoints and finite-solver gradients.

findings: Ho et al. give the finite forward Gaussian Markov chain, closed marginal q(x_t|x_0), posterior q(x_{t-1}|x_t,x_0), and variational decomposition into terminal KL, t>1 Gaussian KLs, and a separate learned decoder term at t=1.

With 0<beta_t<1, each forward noise variance is positive and the posterior variance tilde-beta_t is positive for t≥2. The degenerate conditioned q(x_0|x_1,x_0) is not treated as a Lebesgue density; t=1 uses a separately specified learned decoder with positive variance.

The exact ELBO/negative-log-likelihood identity consumes BCS-22 only with finite positive marginal normalizer, proper posterior, q≪posterior and finite absolute q-log integrability. Every Gaussian conditional consumer of BCS-03 retains PSD joint covariance and strictly positive-definite observed covariance; predictive/posterior covariance may be singular.
L_simple removes ELBO weights and is not maximum-likelihood training. Learned score accuracy, sample quality and finite-step convergence remain empirical.

library_supplier_contracts.contract: For jointly Gaussian (X,Y) with PSD block covariance and observed block Cov(Y)=B≻0, conditional law is Gaussian with mean a+CB^{-1}(y-b) and PSD covariance A-CB^{-1}C^T. For nonnegative density gamma with Z=∫gamma dμ∈(0,∞), proper posterior pi=gamma/Z, probability q≪pi and ∫q(|log gamma|+|log q|)dμ<∞, log Z=ELBO(q)+KL(q||pi). One-way Category 3→4 interface.
Expectation and integrability notation only; does not establish ELBO identity.

findings: Anderson pp. 4–5 explicitly assumes an almost-surely bounded initial state independent of the Brownian process, plus unique smooth forward and joint/conditional KFP densities. Positive-time epsilon truncation does not generally make X_epsilon bounded under Gaussian noising.

ML60 consumes P-SDE-02 for the exact bounded-start Anderson theorem and the separately specified general unbounded-start kernel/martingale design; it does not create a duplicate reverse-time theorem. The unbounded design explicitly names Bayes-reversed kernels, Chapman–Kolmogorov, generator on C_c^infinity, reverse martingale well-posedness/nonexplosion and Brownian reconstruction under uniformly nonsingular sigma.

Anderson’s state-dependent correction is -b+div(a)+a grad(log p); Song’s probability-flow equation requires exact score and regular density evolution, and common score-only formulas are restricted to state-independent scalar diffusion.

The reverse process starts at actual P_T. Finite integrated VP/OU noise generally leaves nonzero residual signal (bar-alpha_T>0); a standard Gaussian prior is an approximation unless matched. Singular t=0 endpoints require separate weak convergence; solver, score and divergence estimation errors remain separate.

source_evidence.citation: Reverse-time Diffusion Equation Models — Brian D. O. Anderson (1982 (Stochastic Processes and their Applications 12, 313–326))

source_evidence.source_claims: For an Itô diffusion with coefficient conditions giving unique strong forward solution and smooth density solving the forward Kolmogorov equation, plus the paper’s smooth unique joint KFP solution, reverse increments yield a Brownian motion after drift adjustment; reverse drift includes density-divergence correction. For state-independent scalar g(t), it reduces to f-g(t)^2 grad log p_t with sign/time convention carefully stated.
source_evidence.hypotheses_and_proof_scope: Smooth/growth coefficient conditions sufficient for forward strong uniqueness; density and joint KFP smoothness/uniqueness assumed or established by cited theory; reverse-time filtration and positive density where score is used. Proof compares joint forward/reverse KFP equations and establishes independent reversed increments and Brownian properties.
source_evidence.source_limits: Does not prove general SDE existence or all density regularity assumptions. Modern score-SDE presentations commonly simplify to g(t); that simplification is not the general state-dependent diffusion formula.

source_evidence.source_limits: Score estimation error, finite prior time, discretization error, and approximate divergence/trace estimation are not controlled by the ideal equations. “Exact likelihood” refers to exact continuous equations, not numerical computation.
